news_summary: IREN heads into its fiscal-year 2026 results (scheduled for August 27, 2026) on a run of AI-cloud momentum confirmed directly on the company's own investor-relations site. On August 13, 2026, IREN announced that Microsoft accepted delivery of 'Horizon 1,' the first of four 50MW direct-to-chip liquid-cooled AI data center deployments under IREN's five-year, $9.7B Microsoft cloud-services contract, and that IREN achieved 'NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud' status following NVIDIA's testing of its GB300 NVL72 deployment at that site; management's stated targets are 480MW (gross) of AI Cloud capacity by year-end 2026 and 1.2GW (gross) by 2027. On August 4, 2026, IREN completed its acquisition of Mirantis, a cloud-software/AI-orchestration company, funded with roughly 12.6 million IREN shares plus about $40 million of cash/RSUs, adding a software/orchestration layer on top of IREN's owned data centers and compute infrastructure. On July 20, 2026, IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI-cloud contracts with additional AI developers, raising its year-end-2026 AI Cloud annualized run-rate revenue (ARR) target from $3.7B to more than $4B, with approximately 85% of that target now under contract.

catalysts.what: Microsoft accepted delivery of Horizon 1, the first of four 50MW direct-to-chip liquid-cooled AI data centers under IREN's five-year, $9.7B Microsoft cloud-services contract; IREN also achieved NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status on its GB300 NVL72 deployment

IREN completed its acquisition of Mirantis (cloud-software/AI-orchestration company) for approximately 12.6 million IREN ordinary shares plus roughly $40 million in cash/RSUs, adding a software layer to its vertically integrated AI Cloud platform

IREN signed $2.8B in new multi-year AI-cloud contracts with additional AI developers, raising its year-end-2026 AI Cloud annualized run-rate revenue (ARR) target from $3.7B to more than $4B, with approximately 85% of that target now under contract
IREN scheduled to release its FY2026 full-year results (fiscal year ended June 30, 2026) via conference call at 5:00pm ET
Management is targeting 480MW (gross) of AI Cloud capacity by year-end 2026, scaling to 1.2GW (gross) by 2027, up from roughly 3MW of self-built AI Cloud capacity a year earlier

move_thesis: IREN's narrative is shifting from a pure bitcoin-mining story to an AI-cloud infrastructure buildout story: rapid, contracted capacity expansion (targeting 480MW gross by year-end 2026 and 1.2GW gross by 2027) anchored by the $9.7B multi-year Microsoft contract, which is now hitting real delivery milestones (Horizon 1 accepted, NVIDIA Exemplar Cloud status). A $2.8B round of new AI-developer contracts lifted the 2026 ARR target above $4B with roughly 85% already under contract, and the Mirantis acquisition adds a software/orchestration layer intended to help IREN serve both hyperscaler bare-metal and managed-cloud customers. The August 27, 2026 FY26 results release is the next scheduled catalyst, where the market will look for confirmation of the capacity ramp pace, the legacy bitcoin-mining segment's contribution, and execution on the remaining Horizon 2-4 deliveries to Microsoft.
